members.name: Dialect
members.doc: Describe a CSV dialect. This must be subclassed (see csv.excel). Valid attributes are: delimiter, quotechar, escapechar, doublequote, skipinitialspace, lineterm

members.name: Error
members.doc: Common base class for all non-exit exceptions.

members.name: excel
members.doc: Describe the usual properties of Excel-generated CSV files.

members.name: excel_tab
members.doc: Describe the usual properties of Excel-generated TAB-delimited files.

members.name: field_size_limit
members.doc: Sets an upper limit on parsed fields. csv.field_size_limit([limit]) Returns old limit. If limit is not given, no new limit is set and the old limit is returned

members.name: get_dialect
members.doc: Return the dialect instance associated with name. dialect = csv.get_dialect(name)

members.name: list_dialects
members.doc: Return a list of all known dialect names. names = csv.list_dialects()

members.name: reader
members.doc: csv_reader = reader(iterable [, dialect='excel'] [optional keyword args]) for row in csv_reader: process(row) The "iterable" argument can be any object that ret

members.name: register_dialect
members.doc: Create a mapping from a string name to a dialect class. dialect = csv.register_dialect(name[, dialect[, **fmtparams]])

members.name: Sniffer
members.doc: "Sniffs" the format of a CSV file (i.e. delimiter, quotechar) Returns a Dialect object.

members.name: StringIO

members.name: unix_dialect
members.doc: Describe the usual properties of Unix-generated CSV files.

members.name: unregister_dialect
members.doc: Delete the name/dialect mapping associated with a string name. csv.unregister_dialect(name)
